### Tool: return_context

Read current subject outputs, bounded Git hunks and exact retained tool payloads, or store revision-bound feedback.

**Endpoints:** /mcp, /mcp/memory. **Category:** self_write.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| action | string | yes |  | {"enum":["outputs","detail","diff","contexts","context","feedback","run_contexts","run_context"]} |
| agent_id | string | no |  | {"maxLength":160,"minLength":1} |
| anchor | object | no |  | {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"end_column":{"maximum":16385,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"end_line":{"maximum":16385,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"expected_diff_revision":{"maxLength":64,"minLength":64,"pattern":"^[0-9a-f]{64}$","type":"string"},"expected_git_revision":{"maxLength":40,"minLength":40,"pattern":"^[0-9a-f]{40}$","type":["string","null"]},"hunk_id":{"maxLength":64,"minLength":64,"pattern":"^[0-9a-f]{64}$","type":"string"},"kind":{"enum":["lines","span","diff_hunk"],"type":"string"},"start_column":{"maximum":16385,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"start_line":{"maximum":16385,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}},"required":["kind"]} |
| comment | string | no |  | {"maxLength":2000,"minLength":1} |
| end_line | integer | no |  | {"minimum":1} |
| expected_revision | string | no |  | {"maxLength":64,"minLength":1} |
| path | string | no |  | {"maxLength":200,"minLength":1} |
| receipt_id | string | no |  | {"maxLength":160,"minLength":1} |
| request_id | string | no |  | {"maxLength":160,"minLength":1} |
| root_id | string | no |  | {"maxLength":160,"minLength":1} |
| start_line | integer | no |  | {"minimum":1} |

**Result:** Current working revisions separate from historical receipts and self-authored reports. Detail includes guarded current named-plan revision/link, up to three immutable publication/recorded-owner references and exact retained helper epochs. Exact bounded tool text retained up to seven days and 100 payloads per actor; emission is server-side only. Diff returns working revision, pinned git_revision, diff_revision and at most 100 identified hunks with explicit has_more_hunks. Raw diff remains on subject_context. Feedback retains typed anchor, selection hash/bytes/preview; detail separately reports content-revision match and current/historical/current_diff_unavailable anchor state.

**Side effects:** Reads current files and historical production/context. Optional diff reads the bounded subject Git snapshot; no source/index/HEAD mutation. Feedback stores comments and at most a 1024-byte exact-selection preview/hash only. Opening never starts or resumes an agent; no source apply, repository approval or merge. New publication receipts capture the exact host-owned helper epoch without native run attribution. Operator run-context reads and lists lazily clear expired stored inline payloads while retaining their metadata.

**Access:** Current configured root/path read grants; private receipt payloads are the requesting actor or human only. Feedback and diff use the exact current path read grant. Feedback binds current revision and inclusive lines, Unicode grapheme span or pinned Git hunk; references do not grant writes. Named current_plan references use current exact document read grants. Private retained helper excerpts require the human or the currently authorized original parent; other root readers get explicit private state. Adapter-entry run receipts require an authenticated operator, including the agent's own receipts.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** Legacy start_line/end_line feedback remains inclusive. Optional anchor.kind is lines, span or diff_hunk, with exact kind-specific keys; mixing top-level lines and anchor refuses. Spans use one-based Unicode grapheme columns and exclusive end; LF/CRLF line separators preserve exact selected bytes without adding a column. Hunk anchors require expected_git_revision (explicit null for unborn), expected_diff_revision and hunk_id from the authorized diff read. Changed source or HEAD/diff refuses with reread/reanchor, even when working bytes still match. Unsupported/missing Git remains unavailable and never labels an old hunk current. The first 100 hunks are reviewable; comments never apply or approve. Preview is at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes on grapheme boundaries with full selection hash/length and explicit truncation. Prepared response is not server emission. Expired payload stays expired; native hidden context and model receipt are unknown. Reused helper ids never retarget historical epochs; missing legacy epochs stay unavailable. Private helper previews use at most three message receipts/two authored reports, 1000 UTF-8 bytes per excerpt and 64KiB navigation. Current plan references are not grants or inferred execution plans. Parent requests and authored reports are not delivery/acceptance proof. Operator-only run_contexts (agent_id) and run_context (receipt_id) inspect exact inline prompt/instruction arguments (including Custode-serialized Codex developer_instructions, with arbitrary credential-bearing overrides omitted) captured at the actual released adapter run:start seam, bound to the matching executing job/generation/turn/configuration/attempt. Adapter entry is not native provider receipt or model use. File-based/native hidden context and turn attribution of MCP reads remain unknown. Payloads retain at most128KiB each, newest100 per agent, with seven-day logical expiry and lazy physical cleanup on capture/read/list; expired, retired or over-budget content never substitutes current bytes. Reads never resume work; earlier turns are not backfilled. Duplicate same-execution captures preserve the first snapshot; conflicting payloads or execution identities refuse. For an admitted helper turn, operator-only run_context detail reports host credential availability at adapter entry and a bounded separate list of retained retrieval receipt links matched to that exact launch/job. Each link preserves prepared or server_emitted state, revision and payload hash; neither credential availability nor server emission proves model receipt/use. Historical receipts survive producer cleanup and do not substitute current document bytes.

### Tool: route_preview

Preview exact configured task routes without changing execution.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** read.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| decision_id | string | no | Read an existing decision instead of previewing a new request. |  |
| request | object | no |  | {"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"candidate_ids":{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":20,"minItems":1,"type":"array"},"class":{"type":"string"},"configured_route":{"type":"string"},"context_provider":{"enum":["claude","codex"],"type":"string"},"context_refs":{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"},"input_revision":{"type":"string"},"isolation":{"enum":["any","read_only","local"],"type":"string"},"limits":{"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"calls":{"maximum":100,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"time_ms":{"maximum":3600000,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"usd":{"exclusiveMinimum":0,"maximum":100,"type":"number"}},"required":["calls","time_ms","usd"],"type":"object"},"phase":{"enum":["plan","execute","verify"],"type":"string"},"pin":{"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"effort":{"type":"string"},"id":{"type":"string"},"model":{"type":"string"},"provider":{"type":"string"}},"type":"object"},"request_id":{"type":"string"},"required_capabilities":{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"},"required_tools":{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"},"task_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["candidate_ids","class","context_refs","input_revision","isolation","limits","phase","request_id","required_capabilities","required_tools","task_id"]} |

**Result:** custode.route_preview.v1: selected/deferred/unsupported_pin, exact configured triple and revisions, effective limits, frozen task inputs, versioned policy, timestamped observations and rejected alternatives.

**Side effects:** Reads current configuration and cached provider observations; atomically persists a frozen shadow decision keyed by request_id. No network probes, prompts, reservations or live routing changes.

**Access:** Authenticated human or configured caretaker, repeated by the shared service. Temporary agents and ordinary owners cannot inspect fleet routes.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** Provide request or decision_id, exclusively. Request fields: request_id, task_id, input_revision, class, phase (plan/execute/verify), candidate_ids, required_tools, required_capabilities, isolation (any/read_only/local), context_refs and limits (calls/usd/time_ms). Optional configured_route, context_provider (native context restriction) and pin (id/provider/model/effort). Exact triples and quality tiers come from operator policy, not caller claims. Unknown/stale capacity cannot win as free capacity. Interactive reserve is a configured fraction, not a live lease. Identical retries return the original decision; changed payload conflicts. Promotion requires a separate natural shadow corpus and authorized evaluation; fixture decisions prove no task quality. A selected preview grants no authority, and execution admission must revalidate current grants/configuration/capacity.

### Tool: run_job

Queue a bounded one-shot task with an inbox completion report.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** delegate.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| elevated | boolean | no | run with full permissions (git, gh, shell). Use ONLY for work a human already approved via a request_permission gate; default is edit-only |  |
| max_budget_usd | number | no | per-run spend cap. Defaults to the shared config default, which is sized for small tasks -- pass your own routine's cap when dispatching implementation work |  |
| max_turns | integer | no | agentic turn cap for the job. Omitted keeps the default (15). Lowering it is always allowed; raising it needs a shell-class approved action in flight whose text names the cap as max_turns=&lt;N&gt;, and the value must be exactly N, within the configured hard ceiling |  |
| model | string | no | claude model (defaults to the configured default) |  |
| prompt | string | yes |  |  |
| report_inbox | string | yes | absolute path of the directory the completion note is written to |  |
| tag | string | no | short label for the completion note |  |
| workspace | string | no | absolute path the job's claude runs in (must exist if given) |  |

**Result:** job_id, absolute reports_to directory and the resolved max_turns.

**Side effects:** Enqueues a one-shot Claude run that can edit files, spend model budget, and write a completion note. Elevated jobs have full shell/Git/GitHub permissions.

**Access:** Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. A routine is limited to its configured working directory or deterministic owned checkout and its own notebook inbox. Elevated routine jobs require a live approved continuation whose action class permits shell work. The human operator may use any existing directories and run elevated jobs directly. Any caller may lower max_turns; raising it above the default requires the operator or a routine with a live approved continuation whose action class permits shell work, the same rule as elevated jobs. That approved action's text must also name the cap with one stable max_turns=&lt;N&gt; marker, and a raised request must equal N exactly, so the approved gate detail names the resolved cap; a missing marker, more than one distinct marker, or a raised request other than N is refused.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** prompt and report_inbox are required; report_inbox and any workspace must already be directories. A routine that omits workspace uses its configured working directory. Lexical and physical path containment prevent traversal and symlink escapes. Path and elevation checks occur before a job is inserted. model and max_budget_usd default to configuration; tag defaults to 'job'. max_turns defaults to run_job_max_turns (15). A named max_turns must be a positive integer no greater than run_job_max_turns_ceiling (150); invalid, zero, over-ceiling or unauthorized values are tool errors and no job is inserted. The configured bounds are validated on every call, including an omitted max_turns: both must be positive integers and the default may not exceed the ceiling, or the call is a tool error and no job is inserted. Runs have a 200000 ms timeout, or 900000 ms when elevated. The completion note's custode-report header carries the resolved max_turns, and a failure note names the turn cap. Acceptance is asynchronous and not idempotent. Final report requires status and summary, with optional artifacts array and cost_note. Eligible explicitly read-only external integrations use a captured immutable catalog config. Elevated permission-bypass jobs do not receive them. Ambient MCP configuration is excluded; captured revision/dispositions are retained in job args.

### Tool: set_next_beat

Request a bounded one-shot change to the next scheduled sweep.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** self_write.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agent_id | string | no | alias for routine_id; either works, and both may be omitted: the server knows who is calling |  |
| minutes | integer | no | minutes from now until your next scheduled beat |  |
| reason | string | no | one line: what you are waiting for |  |
| routine_id | string | no | your own routine id (defaults to the caller) |  |

**Result:** next_beat_at timestamp, granted minutes and clamped boolean.

**Side effects:** Upserts a one-shot scheduling request and records a feed entry. Cron beats are skipped until the requested due time; a started turn clears it.

**Access:** Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. minutes and reason are runtime-required. minutes must be an integer and is clamped to configured bounds, default 5 through 1440. The reply reports the granted time. Operator messages, sensors, inbox events, immediate beats or approvals can start work sooner and clear it. Scheduler availability and other lifecycle rules still apply; this is not an unconditional delivery guarantee. Retrying computes a new deadline relative to the retry time and replaces the previous request.

### Tool: start_agent

Start a persistent helper agent in an existing directory.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** delegate.

Errors include a nonexistent workspace and 'start failed'. Temporary helpers receive eligible captured external read integrations without fleet control or recursive delegation. The memory endpoint also offers caller-filtered integration_list. Newly started Claude helpers use the host subject-assignment enqueue seam. An operator admission may provision a private subject-only configuration for one later exact persisted turn; admission itself grants no ordinary helper rights. Existing helper launches are unchanged until restarted. Scoped turns pin strict MCP discovery and a subject_context allowlist; this is MCP authority, not OS filesystem confinement.

### Tool: subject_assignment

Admit, inspect or revoke one explicit helper subject assignment.

| assignment_id | string | no |  | {"maxLength":160,"minLength":1} |
| destination | string | no |  | {"maxLength":200,"minLength":1} |
| expected_helper_record_id | integer | no |  | {"minimum":1} |
| expected_root_revision | string | no |  | {"maxLength":64,"minLength":1} |
| expires_in_seconds | integer | no |  | {"maximum":3600,"minimum":60} |
| helper_id | string | no |  | {"maxLength":160,"minLength":1} |

**Result:** Admission status, exact helper epoch, original parent, configured root revision, read paths, create-only destination and expiry. Host job and admission-message references are retained separately from unknown native model use.

**Side effects:** Retains operational admission and launch records. Admission alone enables no credential. One later host-enqueued Claude helper turn receives a private subject-only MCP credential. Revocation removes its credential/config without changing files or historical output receipts.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated human operator; routine parents, helpers and unauthenticated calls cannot provision grants.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** admit requires assignment_id, helper_id, root_id, expected_root_revision, expected_helper_record_id, read_paths, destination and expires_in_seconds (60..3600). Expected root revision and helper record ID must match the current host records. The root must already be configured and the helper epoch/current parent valid. At most one unconsumed admission per helper and 1000 retained admissions; reusing an ID with different arguments refuses. New helper launches bind one admission transactionally to one persisted Claude Agent.Job generation/turn/correlation/config identity. Existing helpers retain their old launch configuration and ordinary rights. Every scoped credential invocation rechecks executing attempt1, exact args/meta, current epoch/parent/root revision, expiry and revocation; retries, snoozes and terminal jobs refuse. No inferred workspace rights, arbitrary root selection, directory creation, existing-document apply or Codex helper provisioning. Model receipt/use and OS filesystem confinement remain unknown. A migration/restart is required for the new-helper launch path.

### Tool: subject_context

Bounded access to current working Markdown and scoped local Git history/diff in retained subject roots, with exclusive outputs and revision-bound proposals.

**Endpoints:** /mcp, /mcp/memory. **Category:** self_write.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| action | string | yes |  | {"enum":["roots","browse","read","search","create","propose","receipt","history","diff"]} |
| content | string | no |  | {"maxLength":16384} |
| destination | string | no |  | {"maxLength":200,"minLength":1} |
| expected_revision | string | no |  | {"maxLength":64,"minLength":1} |
| path | string | no |  | {"maxLength":200,"minLength":1} |
| query | string | no |  | {"maxLength":200,"minLength":1} |
| request_id | string | no |  | {"maxLength":160,"minLength":1} |
| root_id | string | no |  | {"maxLength":160,"minLength":1} |

**Result:** custode.subject_roots.v1 or custode.subject_document.v1: root/subject, relative path, observed or published bytes and SHA256 revision, bounded search/browse, root identity and known producer/grant/operation receipt. Current SHA256 revision remains distinct from pinned git_revision; history has path-specific ids/commit timestamps/has_more and no rename following; diff has historical blob id/base content revision versus current working bytes. Unborn/untracked source is explicit. process_memory does not claim hard RSS enforcement. A proposal names its captured source revision, separate destination and applied=false. Refused/unconfirmed outcomes remain durable and idempotent.

**Side effects:** First access pins directory identity in SQLite. Git reads use only a transient private descriptor-copied object snapshot and fixed local built-ins; never change source HEAD/index/files or run configuration, hooks, external diff/textconv, remote or arbitrary commands. Create/propose retain a durable mutation record and exclusively publish a new Markdown file; proposals never replace the source. No commit, publication, worker resume or notebook migration. Ambiguous prepared operations never retry writes automatically.

**Access:** Authenticated human, or a current standing owner/temporary helper with an explicit configured root grant. Helpers require their retained live spawn record and current parent authorization. References do not grant creation. Exact destinations and proposed source paths are separately granted.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** Opt-in subject_roots configuration; default empty. Optional Python 3 POSIX stdlib port holds a directory descriptor and accepts data-only JSON. Canonical relative .md paths in existing directories, up to 200 UTF-8 bytes and eight components; hidden paths, symlinks, traversal, nonregular files and changed root/ancestor directories are refused. 16KiB file, 100-file/500-entry recursive browse, 100KiB search and 5s helper timeout bounds shared across traversal; exact grants prune ungranted subtrees. Over-depth/scan results refuse explicitly. Directory creation and auto apply are unsupported. History/diff use exact current path read grants and never follow renames. Small plain local SHA-1 stores only; linked gitfiles/common stores, alternates, packed deltas and malformed/oversized stores explicitly refuse. Snapshot caps:5000 entries/10MB copied,64KB per expanded object/10MB aggregate,20 history entries with has_more,16KiB historical blob,32KB diff,64KB subprocess output,3.5s operation/2s CPU and bounded pack caches. macOS hard RSS attestation is unavailable; expanded input/cache limits are reported honestly. Git directory/objects/HEAD and held source/ancestors are rechecked before return. Repository author/account metadata and commit prose are omitted. Root authority is its retained directory identity, not a movable pathname or an OS sandbox. Existing native shell tools are unaffected. Source bytes include external uncommitted edits; historical mutation receipts never substitute for current reads. Optional configured current_plan paths are exposed only under current read grants. New helper publications retain a host-owned spawn epoch reference; missing legacy epochs and native delivery attribution remain unavailable. Missing producer execution/session/usage remains unknown. Operator-admitted helper assignments are available only through a host-issued credential for one exact executing Claude job. That credential exposes only subject_context, uses exact admitted read paths and one create destination, and rechecks current job/epoch/parent/root revision/expiry/revocation. Ordinary helper tokens gain no assignment rights. Producer and retrieval receipts retain host assignment/job references separately from unknown native receipt or model use.

### Tool: todo_add

Add a persistent todo.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** self_write.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agent_id | string | no | alias for routine_id; either works, and both may be omitted: the server knows who is calling |  |
| routine_id | string | no | whose list (defaults to the caller) |  |
| text | string | no | the todo, one line |  |

**Result:** todo_id.

**Side effects:** Inserts an open todo, regenerates notebook views and notifies the dashboard.

**Access:** Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. text is runtime-required despite optional discovery schema. Retrying adds another todo. Render destinations use the authorization snapshot for the target's active execution revision, so a mid-turn roster workspace or working_dir edit does not redirect an old turn.

### Tool: todo_complete

Mark an owned todo complete.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** self_write.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| todo_id | integer | yes |  |  |

**Result:** todo_id and status='done'.

**Side effects:** Marks an existing todo done, regenerates notebook views and notifies the dashboard.

**Access:** Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Looks up the todo owner; agents may complete only their own, while the operator may complete any.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** todo_id is required. Unknown IDs fail with 'no todo #&lt;id&gt;'. Completing an already done todo keeps it done but still performs bookkeeping. Render destinations use the authorization snapshot for the todo owner's active execution revision, so a mid-turn roster workspace or working_dir edit does not redirect an old turn.

### Tool: todo_list

Read open, completed or all todos for an identity.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** read.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agent_id | string | no | alias for routine_id; either works, and both may be omitted: the server knows who is calling |  |
| routine_id | string | no | whose list (defaults to the caller) |  |
| status | string | no | one of "open" (default), "done", "all" |  |

**Result:** todos array of id, text and status.

**Side effects:** None.

**Access:** Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Any authenticated caller reaching this tool may read another identity's todos by ID; no self-only read guard.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. status defaults open and is runtime-validated as open, done or all. Oldest todo ID first. No limit input.

### Tool: update_profile

Change a reusable routine profile.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** roster_write.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agent | string | no | new persona |  |
| approve_bypass_permissions | boolean | no | GRANT: bypass_permissions on approval |  |
| approve_effort | string | no | approved-arg effort |  |
| approve_model | string | no | approved-arg model |  |
| approve_worktree | string | no | approved-arg worktree template |  |
| cron | string | no | new default cron |  |
| daily_budget_tokens | integer | no | new daily token rail |  |
| daily_budget_usd | number | no | new daily budget rail |  |
| drop | array | no | envelope keys to REMOVE | {"items":{"type":"string"}} |
| effort | string | no | new effort |  |
| extra_allowed_tools | array | no | GRANT: replacement tool list | {"items":{"type":"string"}} |
| hermetic | boolean | no | seal out ambient persona |  |
| max_budget_usd | number | no | new per-turn budget rail |  |
| max_turns | integer | no | new max turns |  |
| mcp | boolean | no | grant the custode MCP tools |  |
| model | string | no | new model |  |
| name | string | yes | profile name to edit |  |
| prompt | string | no | new default sweep prompt |  |
| provider | string | no | new agent provider: claude or codex |  |
| role | string | no | new role |  |
| sensors | array | no | replacement sensor list | {"items":{"type":"string"}} |
| system_prompt_file | string | no | standing-orders file path |  |
| tags | array | no | replacement tag list | {"items":{"type":"string"}} |
| timeout_ms | integer | no | new per-turn timeout |  |
| working_dir | string | no | new checkout path template |  |
| workspace | string | no | new notebook home template |  |

**Result:** name, configuration path and live=true. Unlike define_profile, this result does not include grants.

**Side effects:** Rewrites the profile, reloads the roster and records a feed entry. Routines inheriting it receive the change on their next run. If the effective provider changes, live wearers are stopped on the old provider and restart on their next beat.

**Access:** Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. A human operator may write directly; a caretaker must also have a live human-approved continuation whose action class is roster. Specialists and temporary agents are refused before configuration changes.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** name is required. provider is claude or codex. Omitted fields remain unchanged; drop removes envelope keys, lists replace, and false bypass does not explicitly revoke an existing grant. Preview the resulting approved_args before writing. Supplying any approve_* values replaces the approved_args envelope rather than merging nested keys. Rewriting removes comments inside the edited section.

### Tool: update_routine

Update an existing routine configuration.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** roster_write.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agent | string | no | persona from the repo's .claude/agents/ (#19) |  |
| cron | string | no | new cron override |  |
| daily_budget_tokens | integer | no | daily token rail |  |
| daily_budget_usd | number | no | new daily budget rail |  |
| drop | array | no | override keys to REMOVE (profile serves again) | {"items":{"type":"string"}} |
| effort | string | no | new effort override, e.g. "low" |  |
| extra_allowed_tools | array | no | extra tool grants, e.g. ["Bash(git log:*)"] | {"items":{"type":"string"}} |
| hermetic | boolean | no | seal out the repo's ambient CLAUDE.md/persona |  |
| id | string | yes | routine id to edit |  |
| max_budget_usd | number | no | new per-turn budget rail |  |
| max_turns | integer | no | new max turns |  |
| mcp | boolean | no | grant the custode MCP tools |  |
| model | string | no | new model override, e.g. "sonnet" |  |
| profile | string | no | new profile name |  |
| prompt | string | no | new sweep prompt |  |
| provider | string | no | new agent provider: claude or codex |  |
| repo | string | no | new owner/name |  |
| role | string | no | role override, e.g. "backlog_worker" |  |
| system_prompt_file | string | no | path to a standing-orders file |  |
| tags | array | no | replacement tag list | {"items":{"type":"string"}} |
| timeout_ms | integer | no | new per-turn timeout |  |
| working_dir | string | no | new checkout path |  |
| workspace | string | no | new notebook home |  |

**Result:** id, path of configuration file, live=true.

**Side effects:** Rewrites configuration, reloads the live roster and records changed field names in the feed. Updated schedule is used by subsequent scheduler checks. A provider change stops the live agent on the old provider; the next beat starts it on the new provider. A repository change starts service for the new repository and can retire the old service if no longer needed.

**Access:** Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. A human operator may write directly; a caretaker must also have a live human-approved continuation whose action class is roster. Specialists and temporary agents are refused before configuration changes.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** id is required and immutable. provider is claude or codex. Omitted fields stay unchanged; lists replace; drop removes overrides and wins over a supplied value. Preview before applying. This response does not promise changes to an already executing turn. Rewriting removes comments inside the edited configuration section; comments in other sections are preserved.

### Tool: workflow_retry_status

Inspect failed-stage replay preconditions without starting work.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Category:** read.

| Argument | Type | Schema required | Description | Other schema constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| run_id | string | yes |  | {"maxLength":160,"minLength":1} |

**Result:** Bounded observed job states, definition/failure binding, and at most100 retained result-validation summaries with truncation. Schema-validated versus legacy/unbound results remain separate from unavailable effect/settlement/budget replay facts. retry_offered is false for current worker contracts.

**Side effects:** Read only. No job enqueue, cancellation, resume, rail raise or file/provider effect.

**Access:** Verified human or current caretaker fleet-control identity. Ordinary owners and temporary helpers cannot read this fleet operation.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** Terminal queue state is not physical settlement; disallowing Write/Edit does not confine Bash or MCP. The read is not atomic retry admission and never offers unsupported replay. New workflow runs capture exact job arguments, pinned policy/package, frozen definition/input/schema and host callback validation receipts; changed or missing bindings cannot be downgraded to legacy. Unsupported schema assertions never become validated receipts. Legacy rows remain unbound. Schema validation is not native execution, physical settlement or reuse authority; absent callback attempts remain explicitly unavailable.

## Resources

### work_attention

`custode://attention`

Derived operator obligations linked to authoritative work state.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A custode.attention.list.v1 page of custode.attention.item.v1 obligations. Items contain subject, reason/evidence, severity/age, owner, authoritative source, and links. The page declares projection.derived=true and projection.independently_mutable=false.

**Side effects:** Read only. Derives obligations afresh; does not acknowledge, resolve, or otherwise mutate them.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator. Other identities do not discover the resource and reads return resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** No arguments. At most 25 items; severity descending, raised time ascending, then attention key ascending. Includes open work gates, blocked WorkItems, latest failed/stale operation calls, and open legacy asks/gates. This is not the list_attention fleet projection. Legacy-agent items can have null resource links. Resolve the source state to remove an obligation.

### work_events

`custode://work-events`

Deterministically paginated append-only WorkEvent history.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A custode.work_event.list.v1 page of custode.work_event.v1 events. Events include actor/operation, before and after state/phase/version, evidence, call/gate and correlation/causation IDs, parent IDs, and timestamp.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not append events, replay work, or change authoritative application state.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator. Other identities do not discover the resource and reads return resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** No arguments. First global page of append-only work-kernel history, at most 25 items; insertion time and event ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri. This is not the routine activity feed.

### work_items

`custode://work-items`

Deterministically paginated WorkItem summaries.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A custode.work_item.list.v1 page of custode.work_item.summary.v1 items across Missions. Includes state and workflow phase separately, priority/version, current Attempt, open gates, unexpired relevant artifacts, last transition, compatibility metadata, and timestamps.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not advance WorkItems, run Attempts, or change authoritative application state.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator. Other identities do not discover the resource and reads return resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** No arguments. First global page, at most 25 items, ordered by insertion time then WorkItem ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri. This is the frozen work-kernel model, not the routine roster or current agent execution list.

### work_missions

`custode://missions`

Deterministically paginated Mission summaries.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A custode.mission.list.v1 page of custode.mission.summary.v1 items. Summaries include identity, purpose, lifecycle/status, targets, policy/budget/context references, work counts by state, last transition, compatibility metadata, and timestamps.

**Side effects:** Read only. Computes a projection from stored records; does not create Missions, schedule work, or change authoritative application state.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Listed and readable for an authenticated operator; routine and sub-agent identities see no resource and reads return resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** No arguments. First page, at most 25 items. Ordered by insertion time and Mission ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri. The work-kernel intake is frozen, but compatibility Mission records for active routines can still exist.

## Resource templates

### mission_work_items

`custode://missions/{mission_id}/work-items`

List WorkItems belonging to one Mission.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** The first custode.work_item.list.v1 page restricted to one Mission; items use the same summary contract as work_items.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not create or schedule WorkItems.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** mission_id is the required opaque public Mission identifier. The Mission must exist; unknown IDs return resource-not-found. At most 25 items, ordered by insertion time and WorkItem ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri.

### mission_work_items_page

`custode://missions/{mission_id}/work-items/pages/{cursor}`

Continue one Mission's WorkItem list using its opaque cursor.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A continuation custode.work_item.list.v1 page restricted to the named Mission.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not change authoritative application state.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** mission_id is the required opaque public Mission identifier; cursor is a required token from that Mission's preceding WorkItem page. Percent-encode each segment or follow page.next_uri. Unknown Mission returns resource-not-found. A cursor from another Mission or global WorkItem list returns invalid-params. At most 25 items.

### work_attention_page

`custode://attention/pages/{cursor}`

Continue the derived Attention projection using its opaque cursor.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A continuation custode.attention.list.v1 page of derived operator obligations, with the same item and projection fields as work_attention.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not acknowledge or resolve obligations.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** cursor is the required opaque token from a preceding Attention page. Invalid cursors return invalid-params. At most 25 items. Attention is recomputed on each read, so continuation is not a frozen snapshot of obligations. Legacy asks and gates are included.

### work_events_page

`custode://work-events/pages/{cursor}`

Continue global append-only WorkEvent history using its opaque cursor.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A continuation custode.work_event.list.v1 page across all WorkItems.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not append or replay events.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** cursor is the required opaque token from a preceding global WorkEvent page. WorkItem-scoped event cursors cannot be reused here. Invalid or cross-scope cursors return invalid-params. At most 25 events.

### work_item_artifacts

`custode://work-items/{work_item_id}/artifacts`

List all Artifacts belonging to a WorkItem.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A custode.artifact.list.v1 page of custode.artifact.v1 metadata, including ID/kind/producer, external identity, digest/media type, location/size, retention/expiry/provenance, parent IDs, and timestamps.

**Side effects:** Read only. Reads artifact metadata; does not open, download, validate, or mutate the artifact bytes at the location.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found. Includes all stored artifacts, including expired records, unlike relevant_artifacts in WorkItem summaries. At most 25 items ordered by insertion time and artifact ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri.

### work_item_artifacts_page

`custode://work-items/{work_item_id}/artifacts/pages/{cursor}`

Continue one WorkItem's Artifact list using its opaque cursor.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A continuation custode.artifact.list.v1 metadata page for the WorkItem.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not read or modify artifact bytes or authoritative state.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier; cursor is a required continuation token from that same WorkItem's artifact collection. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found. Invalid or cross-scope cursor returns invalid-params. At most 25 metadata records.

### work_item_attempt

`custode://work-items/{work_item_id}/attempt`

Read the explicit active or newest logical Attempt for a WorkItem.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A custode.work_item.current_attempt.v1 object containing mission_id, work_item_id, a nullable detailed attempt, and links. Attempt details include provider/profile, state/timing, context IDs/digest, provenance/usage/continuation, job/workflow identifiers, outcome and errors.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not create, resume, or run an Attempt.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found; an existing WorkItem without an Attempt returns attempt=null. Selects the explicitly active Attempt if set, otherwise the newest logical Attempt. Check attempt.active before treating it as live execution.

### work_item_detail

`custode://work-items/{work_item_id}`

Read one WorkItem by its stable opaque identifier.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A custode.work_item.detail.v1 object. Adds objective/acceptance criteria, source/external key/policy, active Attempt/call IDs, waiting/blocked conditions, outcome and terminal timestamps, full nested current Attempt/open gates/relevant artifacts, relationship IDs, and navigation links to the summary fields.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not advance work, start an Attempt, or resolve a gate.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier. Unknown IDs return resource-not-found. State and workflow phase have different meanings and remain separate. relevant_artifacts excludes expired records; the dedicated artifact collection includes them.

### work_item_events

`custode://work-items/{work_item_id}/events`

Read one WorkItem's append-only transition and process history.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** The first custode.work_event.list.v1 page restricted to the WorkItem's transition and process history.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not append, replay, or modify events.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found. At most 25 events ordered by insertion time and event ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri. This is kernel event history, not provider conversation history.

### work_item_events_page

`custode://work-items/{work_item_id}/events/pages/{cursor}`

Continue one WorkItem's WorkEvent history using its opaque cursor.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A continuation custode.work_event.list.v1 page restricted to the WorkItem.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not append, replay, or modify events.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier; cursor is a required token from that WorkItem's preceding event page. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found. Invalid or wrong-scope cursor returns invalid-params. At most 25 events.

### work_items_page

`custode://work-items/pages/{cursor}`

Continue a WorkItem list using its opaque cursor.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A continuation custode.work_item.list.v1 page across all Missions.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not change authoritative application state.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** cursor is a required opaque token from a preceding global WorkItem page. It cannot be reused from a Mission-scoped list. Percent-encode it or follow page.next_uri. Invalid cursors return invalid-params. At most 25 items.

### work_mission_detail

`custode://missions/{mission_id}`

Read one Mission by its stable opaque identifier.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** A custode.mission.detail.v1 object: summary fields plus retention, metadata, relationship IDs for WorkItems/Attempts/calls/gates/artifacts/events, and self/work_items links.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not create or modify the Mission or its related records.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** mission_id is the required opaque public Mission identifier, not a database row number. Percent-encode it as one path segment. Unknown IDs return resource-not-found. Mission records can be compatibility projections for active routines while work-kernel intake is frozen.

### work_missions_page

`custode://missions/pages/{cursor}`

Continue a Mission list using its opaque cursor.

**Endpoints:** /mcp. **Media type:** application/json.

**Result:** The next custode.mission.list.v1 page with the same item and navigation shape as work_missions.

**Side effects:** Read only. Does not change authoritative application state.

**Access:** Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.

**Behavior, defaults and errors:** cursor is the required opaque continuation token from the preceding Mission page. Percent-encode the segment or use page.next_uri directly. At most 25 items. Invalid or wrong-collection cursors return invalid-params.

## Prompts

No MCP prompts are currently registered on either endpoint.
